A local SEO audit is a check of how well your business shows up when people search for something near them. It looks at your Google Business Profile, your website, your listings, your reviews and your links, and it ends with a list of fixes in order of importance.

This guide gives you a 12-step local SEO audit you can do yourself, with a checklist, a worked example, a report template and the tools you need. It works for shops, clinics, restaurants, trades, agencies and any business that serves customers in a set area.

What is a local SEO audit?

A local SEO audit is a structured review of the things that decide whether your business appears in Google's local results, Google Maps and AI answers for searches such as "plumber near me" or "accountant in Leeds."

It answers four questions:

  • Can searchers find you, and is the information about you correct?
  • Do you look trustworthy compared with nearby rivals?
  • Does your website match what local searchers want?
  • What should you fix first?

Why should you run a local SEO audit?

  • Wrong details lose customers. A wrong phone number or old opening hours sends people to a rival.
  • Local results change. New rivals, new reviews and new Google features change who appears.
  • It shows quick wins. Most audits find simple fixes that take hours, not weeks.
  • It guides your budget. You see which fix is worth your time first.
  • It sets a baseline. You can measure progress against it.

Run a full audit once a year and a short check every quarter.

What does a local SEO audit include?

AreaWhat you check
Google Business ProfileName, address, phone, category, hours, services, photos, posts and questions
Citations and listingsWhether your details are correct and the same across directories
ReviewsNumber, rating, recent activity and how you reply
WebsiteLocal pages, titles, content, speed, mobile layout and schema
LinksLocal and relevant sites that link to you
Rankings and visibilityWhere you appear for local searches, on the map and in normal results
CompetitorsWhat the top businesses do that you do not
TrackingWhether you can see calls, direction requests and form fills

How does Google decide who appears in local results?

Google says local results are based mainly on three things: relevance, distance and prominence. Knowing them helps you read your audit.

Relevance is how well your profile matches what the person searched for. A complete profile with the right categories and clear services helps Google see that you fit the search. Distance is how far your business is from the searcher, or from the place named in the search. You cannot change where you are, but you can make sure your address and service area are right. Prominence is how well known your business is. It comes from reviews, links, mentions and how often people search for you by name. Google also says that good SEO practice helps your website's role in local ranking.

This is why the audit covers so many areas. The profile feeds relevance. The address feeds distance. Reviews, links and citations feed prominence. A gap in one of them can hold back the others.

Service-area businesses and more than one location

Some businesses go to the customer, such as plumbers, cleaners and mobile mechanics. These are called service-area businesses. They can hide their street address on their profile and list the areas they serve instead. The audit for them has two extra checks. First, confirm that the service areas match the places where you really work and do not list more than you can cover. Second, make sure your website has a page for each main area, with real detail about that area, such as typical jobs, local landmarks and customer comments.

If you have several locations, audit each one. Every site should have its own profile, its own page and its own reviews. Keep one row per location in your spreadsheet with its profile status, review count, rating, local page and monthly calls. This makes it easy to see which site needs the most work, and it stops one good location from hiding a weak one.

How to read your reviews like an auditor

When you read reviews for the audit, do not stop at the star rating. Look at the words customers use. If several reviews say "fast reply" or "clean and tidy," those are things you can put on your website and use as proof. If several mention long waits or unclear prices, those are problems to fix in the business, and no amount of SEO will cover them up.

Also look at how rivals reply. A calm, short reply that names the problem and offers to fix it shows future customers how you treat people. Copy that approach. Avoid long arguments, and never share private details about a customer in a public reply. Aim for a steady flow of new reviews rather than a burst, since a burst can look odd and a steady flow shows an active business.

How to write a local title and description

The page title is one of the clearest signals of what a page is about, and it is the first thing a searcher sees. For local pages, put the service first, then the place, then your name. Keep it near 60 characters so it is not cut off in the results.

For example, a weak title is "Home | Smith and Sons." A better one is "Emergency Plumber in Leeds | Smith and Sons." The second tells both people and search engines what the page is for and where. The meta description is the short text under the title. Use it to say what you offer, where and why to call, in a sentence or two. A good one reads like a helpful answer, not a list of keywords.

What local schema markup looks like

Schema markup is code that you add to a page to describe it to search engines. For a local business, it states the business type, name, address, phone number, opening hours, the areas you serve and links to your profiles. It does not change what visitors see. It helps search engines read the page correctly. Many SEO plugins for WordPress and other platforms can add it for you. In the audit, check that the details in the markup match your profile and your page exactly, since a mismatch sends mixed signals.

How voice and mobile searches change the audit

Many local searches are made on a phone, often while walking or driving, and some are spoken to an assistant. People use full questions such as "Where can I find a plumber open now?" Your audit should test for this. Check that your hours are correct and easy to find, that your phone number is clickable, that your pages answer common questions in plain words and that your address is easy to copy into a map. Short answers near the top of a page and a short FAQ section help here, since they match how people ask.

Before you start: what you need

  • Your exact business name, address and phone number (NAP) as you want it shown
  • Access to your Google Business Profile, website and Google Search Console
  • A spreadsheet for notes, with one tab for each area
  • A list of five to ten searches a customer would use, such as "[service] in [town]"
  • Your three closest local rivals

Use a private browser window when you search, so your history changes the results less. Also check from a phone, because local searches are often made on one.

Step 1: Check your Google Business Profile

This is the most important step for most local businesses. Open your profile and check every field.

FieldWhat good looks like
Business nameYour real name, with no added keywords
Primary categoryThe one that best describes your main service
Other categoriesA few that are true for your business
Address and service areaCorrect, and the service area matches where you really work
Phone and websiteCorrect, working, with a link to the right page
HoursCurrent, including holiday hours
Services or productsListed with short, plain descriptions
PhotosRecent, real photos of the place, team and work
Posts and updatesRecent
Questions and answersCommon questions answered

Fix what is wrong as you go. Check also that no duplicate profile exists for the same business, since duplicates split reviews and confuse customers.

Step 2: Check your NAP and citations

A citation is any online mention of your business name, address and phone number, such as a directory listing. Search engines compare these to confirm your details.

  1. Search your business name and phone number in Google and note every listing that appears.
  2. Check the main ones: Google, Bing Places, Apple Maps, Facebook, Yelp where it applies, and the top directories for your trade or country.
  3. Write the details you find in a table and mark any that differ.
  4. Fix wrong details, and remove or merge duplicates.

Small differences count. "Street" and "St." or a different suite number can look like a different business. Use one format and repeat it exactly.

Step 3: Audit your reviews

Reviews affect both ranking and whether a customer picks you.

  • Count and rating. Compare your number of reviews and your average with the three rivals.
  • Recent activity. A page of old reviews looks stale. Look for reviews in the last three months.
  • Replies. Check whether you reply to reviews, good and bad, in a calm and short way.
  • Themes. Read the reviews for patterns: what customers praise and what they complain about.
  • Your process. Do you ask every customer for a review? A direct link by text or email makes it easy.

Do not buy reviews or write your own. Review platforms can remove them, and some countries treat fake reviews as unfair practice.

Step 4: Check your local keywords

Local keywords combine a service with a place, such as "emergency plumber Leeds" or "family lawyer near me." Do this:

  1. List your main services and the places you serve.
  2. Use a keyword tool to check volume for each combination.
  3. Search the top ones in Google and note who appears in the map results and in the normal results.
  4. Note which searches your business already appears for in Search Console.

Match each important keyword to one page on your site. If you have no page for a service or place that matters, add it to your fix list.

Step 5: Audit your website for local SEO

Open your site on a phone and on a computer. Check these things.

Pages

  • A page for each main service
  • A page for each location, with its own address, hours, map and details
  • A contact page with your NAP, a map and a form

Titles and headings

  • Each page title names the service and the place, and is under about 60 characters
  • Each page has one main heading and clear subheadings

Content

  • Real local detail: areas you serve, local examples, parking, landmarks and local reviews
  • No copied pages with only the town name swapped

Speed and mobile

  • Pages load fast on a phone
  • Click-to-call number and clear buttons

Schema markup

  • Local business data with your name, address, phone, hours and area served

Step 6: Check your map and local pack position

The local pack is the box of three businesses with a map at the top of many local results. Check where you appear.

  • Search each key local phrase from a phone, in a private window.
  • Note whether you appear in the pack, in Maps or only in the normal results.
  • Note who appears instead and what is different about them: reviews, distance, categories, photos or website.

Results change with the searcher's location. A business a few streets closer to the searcher may rank higher. That is normal. Look at the pattern across several searches, not one.

Step 7: Check your local links

Links from relevant local sites help you rank. Check who links to you and who links to your rivals.

  • Look for local news, chambers of commerce, trade bodies, schools, charities and local blogs
  • Note links your rivals have that you lack
  • Note any links from poor or unrelated sites

Plan honest ways to earn links: sponsor a local event, join your trade body, offer an expert tip to a local paper or partner with a nearby business. Do not buy links. Google's spam policies treat buying links to affect rankings as link spam.

Step 8: Check your competitors

Compare yourself with the three businesses that appear most often for your key searches. Use a table.

CheckYouRival ARival BRival C
Number of reviews
Average rating
Number of photos
Categories used
Service pages on the website
Location pages
Recent posts or updates

Fill it in. The gaps tell you what to do first.

Step 9: Check your tracking

If you cannot measure results, you cannot tell what works.

  • Is Google Search Console connected and verified?
  • Is Google Analytics set up with events for calls, form submissions and clicks on directions?
  • Do you use a call tracking number or ask customers how they found you?
  • Do you review the Business Profile performance report, which shows calls, direction requests and website clicks?

Step 10: Check technical basics

  • Indexing. Your key pages should appear in Google. Search for your page title in quotes to check.
  • HTTPS. The whole site should load securely.
  • Broken links and pages. Fix or redirect them.
  • Duplicate content. Merge near-copies.
  • Accessibility. Readable text, good contrast, labelled forms.

Step 11: Check AI search visibility

More people ask AI tools for local options. Test it yourself.

  1. Ask ChatGPT, Google's AI answers and another AI tool the questions a customer would ask, such as "best family dentist in [town]."
  2. Note whether your business appears, what is said about it and whether the details are correct.
  3. Note the sources the tools use, such as review sites or directories.

If details are wrong, fix them at the source: your profile, your site and your listings. There is no way to force an AI tool to name you, but accurate facts, good reviews and clear pages help.

Step 12: Write your fix list

Put every issue in a table with three columns: the problem, the impact and the effort. Then sort.

PriorityTypeExamples
1High impact, low effortWrong phone number, missing category, no review request process
2High impact, higher effortNew service pages, location pages, review growth plan
3Lower impact, low effortAdd photos, answer questions on your profile, fix small listing errors
4Longer termLink building, content program, reporting setup

Work from the top. Re-check after 30 days.

A worked example: a plumbing company

This example is illustrative. A plumbing company with one office covers three towns. It runs the 12 steps and finds this.

AreaFindingFix
ProfilePrimary category is "Contractor"Change to "Plumber" and add "Water heater installer" as another
CitationsTwo directories show an old phone numberCorrect both and merge one duplicate
ReviewsFewer reviews than two rivals, no repliesSend a review link after each job and reply to all reviews
WebsiteOne page for all services, no town pagesCreate separate pages for the three main services and one for each town
LinksNo local linksJoin the trade body and sponsor a local youth team with a link
TrackingNo call trackingSet up call events and ask new customers how they found the company

The owner fixes the first three rows in one week. The new service and town pages take a month. After 90 days, the company repeats the audit and compares calls and direction requests with the first month.

Local SEO audit tools

Tool typeExamplesUse
Google toolsGoogle Business Profile, Search Console, AnalyticsFree, accurate data on your own performance
Local SEO suitesBrightLocal, Semrush, Moz Local, Whitespark and similarCitation checks, rank tracking by location and review monitoring
Site crawlersScreaming Frog, Sitebulb and similarFind technical problems across your pages
Speed testsPageSpeed InsightsCheck mobile loading

You can do a good first audit with free tools only. Paid tools save time when you manage many locations or clients.

What goes in a local SEO audit report?

If you share the audit with a boss, a client or a team, keep the report short and clear.

  1. Summary. Three or four sentences: the main findings and the top actions.
  2. Scorecard. A simple rating for each area, for example good, needs work, urgent.
  3. Findings. One short section per area with screenshots.
  4. Competitor comparison. The table from step 8.
  5. Action plan. The prioritized fix list, with owners and dates.
  6. Next review date. Usually in 30 to 90 days.

How long does a local SEO audit take?

A small business with one location can finish a first pass in a day. Several locations, or a large site, can take a week or more. The fixes take longer than the audit. Google says changes can take hours to months to show, so give them time and check progress in 30, 60 and 90 days.

Common local SEO audit mistakes

  • Looking only at the website. For local searches, the Business Profile often matters more.
  • Checking from one place. Results vary by location and device.
  • Ignoring reviews. They shape both ranking and choice.
  • Fixing nothing. An audit is only useful if you act on it.
  • Fixing everything at once. Work in priority order and measure.
  • Skipping the follow-up. Repeat the checks every quarter.

A quick local SEO audit checklist

  • Profile complete, correct category, hours and services
  • NAP identical across listings, no duplicates
  • Steady reviews and replies to all of them
  • A page for each main service and each location
  • Titles with service and place, local schema, fast mobile pages
  • A few honest local links
  • Calls, directions and form fills tracked
  • Checked in Google, Maps and AI tools
  • A prioritized fix list and a date for the next audit

Final thoughts

A local SEO audit shows where customers lose you and where they can find you. Do the 12 steps, fix the high-impact items first and check again in a month. Repeat the audit each year, and keep a short quarterly check in your calendar.

How To Find Your Target Audience on Instagram

01. Start with Making Most Accurate Buyer Persona

 

81% of users say they use the platform to research products and services.

So if you desire to sell your services to appropriate customers, a buyer persona is a must.

A buyer persona is a researched and predicted profile that is later used to serve target customers properly.

To make an ideal buyer persona, you need to collect all the information about a particular person:

  1. Age
  2. Gender
  3. Location
  4. Occupation
  5. Monthly income
  6. Education level
  7. Other interests

All the information is enough to make a buyer persona for your business.

But before making the persona, you need to have a clear idea of your own business.

To get a clear idea of your business, you’ve got to ask yourself these four questions first:

  1. What is my product?
  2. What audience do I want to attract? (Or, who is my product designed for?)
  3. What is my audience looking for?
  4. How am I going to attract that audience?

If you get answers to all these questions, it can be really easy for you to make your buyer personas.

So before thinking about growing at Instagram with your business, do not even think of skipping this option.

Start with your buyer persona and make your services best suitable for all your target customers on Instagram.

 

02. Analyze your Niche Competitors

An effectual answer for ‘how to find your target audience on Instagram’

 

7 out of 10 US Companies are Already Using Instagram. (Neal Schaffer)

If you find all these answers, then think that selecting the target audience on Instagram problem is already done.

03. Monitor Instagram Demographics Regularly

 

200 million users check out at least one business profile each day.

04. Never Forget to Stalk your own Followers

Instagram users spent an average of 30 minutes per day on the platform.

post_title: How to use keywords in Content
meta: How to use keywords in Content

post_content:
Do you know how to use keywords or how to use long-tail keywords in Content? If you are looking for the answer, you are in the right place. 

Using the keywords properly is a significant part of SEO and content writing. When you want to rank your content for a specific keyword, there is no alternative to using keywords properly. 

There are certain methods of keyword use that we will share with you.

But we will discuss how placing keywords in the content can be your trump card.

There are some secret tips that will help you to rank faster than ever, and it’s completely suggested practice. 

 

Let’s jump into a complete guide to keyword placement- where to use keywords for SEO. Before that, we will start with some basic concepts. 

 

What is a keyword? 

 

A keyword can be any word that people search on the internet. This is a basic definition, but we are not going to explain only with the traditional definition; let’s start with an example. 

 

You may search: Nugget recipe 

And here is the answer in the SERP.

This “nugget recipe” is a keyword, and the ranked blogs are about how to make nuggets. Now think again; you may also search for it as “how to make nuggets”. And here is the result. 

Though all results are not the same, you will get similar info on the SERP page. Now, what about writing it differently? Well, we can search for “nugget making process”. Here is the result: 

As you can see, whatever you search is a keyword, and though the search intent is the same, the variation of words can change the SERP result. 

 

You can ask, how many types of keywords are available? Well, you can decide in many ways. like, based on the character count- we decide them as 

 

  • Short-tail keywords 
  • Long-tail keywords 

 

We have already shown the example, nugget recipe is a short-tail keyword, and how to make nugget is a long-tail one.

When you want to learn about how to use keywords in Content, you should know how to use both long-tail and short-tail keywords in Content and short-tail. 

 

We can create a type of keyword in another way based on the search intent. They are: 

  • Informative Keywords 
  • Navigational keywords 
  • Commercial Keywords
  • Transitional Keywords 

 

Here is a detail; check it out!

What is keyword research? 

 

This is another basic concept and one of the most popular words in SEO, Keyword research. Keyword research is a key factor of SEO, no doubt.

If you ask what keyword research is, the easiest way to explain it is finding out how people search a particular topic. 

 

Let me give you an example. Suppose you have a website on the beauty and skin care niche.

You want to sell skincare and makeup products. Now, how can keyword research help? 

 

You will find out how people are searching on the internet about makeup products and skin care.

Use the keywords in your content, optimize it, and it will appear in the search results.

That’s how it works, well not in this much simple way, there are complications. You can read this blog about: 

 

If you use short-tail, highly competitive keywords, then you may have to use the keywords more often. You cannot avoid it even if you want to.

There is a standard number, 2 Percent, but it doesn’t always work.

So when you are targeting a keyword, short tail and high difficulty, you can use the focus keyword about 10 times in 1000 words.

Again, this is not a static number that you must follow. This is for your convenience so that you can make an assumption.

 

Hope you have understood how to do keyword research.

 

What is keyword Stuffing? 

 

 

Keyword using and keyword Stuffing are closely related to each other. When you use your keywords in your content, it helps the search engine to understand the topic.

But what if you use the keywords too much? Well, this is called keyword stuffing, which is completely harmful for SEO. 

But how do you get rid of keyword Stuffing? It sounds easy, because you may think “I will not use them too much”.

Well, that’s not how it can always be solved.

Because sometimes, you need to use the keywords because of the context. You have to use them to make the topic understandable. 

Now the question is, how to solve the issue? There are some steps you may follow to get rid of the keyword Stuffing issue: 

  • Make a plan for how many times you are going to use the keywords. 
  • Find out the synonyms of the keywords. If you have to use the keywords more than the expected number, use them. 

Remember, keyword Stuffing is harmful to SEO. A few years ago, we saw people using it as a trick, and it worked.

Google ranked the content with keyword Stuffing. But with the updates of the Search engine, the sites got penalized, and it is going on.

So, if you do not want to face any trouble, do not do keyword Stuffing. We have a detailed article about keyword Stuffing; read it for more information. 

 

What is Keyword stuffing? 

 

What is keyword difficulty? 

 

 

Keyword difficulty is one of the common words as well, we can see it everywhere about keyword research.

In a basic sense, how difficult it is to rank a keyword is called keyword difficulty. To learn more about it, read our blog about : 

What is keyword difficulty?

How to use keywords in Content? 

 

You have to use keyword phrases following some basic rules while creating content: 

  • You cannot do keyword Stuffing 
  • You have to use them accordingly 
  • Use the less difficult keywords to rank faster

These are basic rules that you must follow. But you need to know where and how to use the keywords in a blog post, right?

 

Keywords in Title Tag:

 

 

Using your primary keyword is recommended and helpful for SEO.

So, when your content appears in a search query, it helps the reader to understand what your blog is about. It also helps to appear in voice searches.

 

 

Keywords in the introduction:

 

Using keywords in the introductory paragraph or head term is the best practice of search engine optimization.

You have to use the main keywords or focus keyword at least once in the first 100 words.

We suggest using the keywords right in the first line, However, you can use it later also, but must be in the first 100 words.

Using keywords inthe  introduction is significant because: 

  • It helps the reader to understand what you are writing about. 
  • Search engine crawlers can understand your context easily. 
  • It amplifies your ranking factor. 

 

Keywords in the meta description:

 

Meta description is an important part, this is what a user sees first when they search for something. So you have to use the keywords in the meta description part. As the meta description is only 160 characters, you can use keywords only once. 

Keywords in the body:

 

We always get questions: How to use keywords in the body? How many times should we use the focus keyword in the body? Well, the answer is not static; there is no magic number. Because: 

 

  • If you use short-tail, highly competitive keywords, then you may have to use the keywords more often.

         There is a standard number, 2 Percent, but it doesn’t always work.

          So when you are targeting a keyword, short tail and high difficulty, you can use the focus keyword about 10 times in 1000 words.

          Again, this is not a static number that you must follow. 

  • When you are targeting a long tail and less competitive keywords, you can use the keyword 2 or 3 times in the body; that is enough and will not make any stuffing.
  • You can use paid & free tools to count the number of keywords.

 

Keywords in the conclusion:

 

For the conclusion, endnote, or wrapping up whatever you say, use the keyword once in the last 100 words.

It means a lot and is a very helpful tactic for SEO. And if you are targeting a short-tail keyword, you can use it more than once.

However, your total keyword usage should be maintained with the word count. 

Number of Words and Keyword Use:

 

Last but not least, keyword use varies with the number of words of the content.

If your blog is 2000 words, then you may use the focus keyword 6/7 times.

But will it be the same in the case of the 1000-word Content? Of course not! It will differ.  It will be less. 

Using Secondary Keywords or LSI: There can be many keywords that you are not focusing on, but as they are related to the topic, you will cover them also. Let’s give an example: 

Your focus keyword is: Best Mobile phone under 100 dollars. 

Here, you can cover different topics related to the main context. Your secondary keyword or LSI keyword can be: 

-Mobile phone price 

-Cheap Mobile phone 

-Smart phone price 

When you want to learn about how to use keywords in content writing, here comes the question: how many LSI keywords you use? 

There are different opinions about it. But we got good results using them 1 or 2 times in the content. Each keyword in one content, it helps to rank in different keywords. 

Keywords in Anchor Text: You can also use your keywords in the anchor text of your internal and external links.

But do not use the main keyword; try to use the LSI keywords in the anchor text.

If you use the focus keyword, it may accelerate the bounce rate and lower the user experience as well as lose your target audience.

 

Semantically Related Keywords: There may be some short-tail keywords that are related to your context.

Enriching your content by using them can help a lot to make it easier to rank.

Maintain it on all pages of your site. You can find them out easily with the SEMRush Tool.

But manually finding out is a little bit complicated. We will post a blog about it soon! 

Read more about it here: What are semantically related words?

Wrapping Up 

Hope you have a good idea about how to use keywords in Content and how many times you should use.

Do not do keyword Stuffing, and use them properly. If you write good-quality content, then you can appear in Google search results easily.

Good-quality content always includes keyword optimization because it is an integral part of SEO.

post_title: How to write SEO friendly blog posts
meta: How to write SEO friendly blog posts

post_content:
To write SEO friendly blog posts, pick one topic that a real person searches for, check what already ranks and what it misses, then write a clear, original answer with a unique title, short sections, proof, useful links and a plain description. Put the answer first, name the author, cite sources you have read, and update the post when the facts change. Search engines reward content made for people, so the best SEO step is to be more useful than what is already there.

This guide gives you 12 steps in the order we use them, the data on why most posts get no search traffic, a checklist you can copy, and a worked example. It replaces our older post on the same topic. We cite only sources we could read at the publisher, and we say where a figure is a vendor's own study.

What is an SEO friendly blog post?

It is a post that is useful to a reader and easy for a search engine to find, read and understand. The two goals fit together. Google says SEO can be a helpful activity when it is applied to people-first content, but not when the content is made mainly to attract search visits.

An SEO friendly post has six traits:

  • One clear topic and one primary keyword that match a real search need.
  • A unique, accurate title and a direct answer near the top.
  • Original value: first-hand experience, examples or data that other pages lack.
  • Clear headings, short sentences and easy-to-scan sections.
  • Honest signals of trust: an author, sources and a date that means something.
  • Good links, useful images and a page that loads fast on a phone.

Why do most blog posts get no search traffic?

Ahrefs, an SEO software vendor, studied about 14 billion pages in its own index. It found that 96.55% of pages get no traffic from Google, and 1.94% get one to ten visits a month. Ahrefs notes that the sample leans toward the quality side of the web and that its traffic numbers are estimates, so the real share may differ. Its newer statistics roundup says only 1.74% of newly published pages reach the top 10 for at least one keyword within a year, and that 72.9% of pages in the top 10 are more than three years old.

These figures do not mean blogging is pointless. They mean that publishing alone is not enough. Posts that earn traffic usually match what people want, add something new, and get links and time. That is the aim of the steps below.

12 steps to write SEO friendly blog posts

Step 1: Choose a topic with real value

Start with your customers, not a keyword list. Ask: Is this a question my audience has? Can I add something that others have not? If I rank, will it help my business? Then use keyword research to check demand and to choose the words people use. Pick one primary keyword for each post and two or three related phrases or questions. A tool such as Semrush or Ahrefs helps, and free sources such as Google Search Console, autocomplete and "People also ask" are a good start.

Step 2: Check search intent and study the top results

Search your keyword and read the top 10 pages on the search engine results page (SERP). Note what kind of page ranks: a how-to, a list, a comparison, a tool or a definition. Note what each page covers and what it leaves out. Your post must fit the intent. If everyone ranking is a step-by-step guide, a long opinion piece will struggle. Then plan what you can add: a fresher statistic, a worked example, a table, an expert view or a question the others skip. We run this check on every post before we write.

Step 3: Write a unique, accurate title

Google's guidance says a good title is unique to the page, clear and concise, and accurately describes the content. Put the primary keyword near the front and aim for about 60 characters so it is less likely to be cut off. Avoid exaggeration. Google's quality questions ask whether the main heading avoids being shocking or overstated. Do not expect your title to show exactly as written. Ahrefs found that Google rewrote title tags 33.4% of the time in its study, and that it was more likely to rewrite titles that were too long. When Google ignored the title tag, it used the H1 about half the time, so make your H1 and title agree.

Step 4: Start with the answer

Give the main answer in the first two or three sentences, then explain. Readers get what they need fast. Search engines and AI answer tools can also pull a clean answer from the page. Semrush recommends starting each section with a direct answer for the same reason. Skip long warm-ups that say nothing new.

Step 5: Outline with one H1 and clear H2 and H3 headings

Use one H1 for the title. Use H2 headings for the main sections and H3 headings for the parts within them. Write headings that say what the section answers, and where it fits, use a question that people ask, such as "How long should a blog post be?" This helps people scan, and it shows search engines how the page is organized. Do not skip levels or use headings only for style.

Step 6: Add original value

This step matters most. Google asks whether content provides original information, reporting, research or analysis, and whether it adds substantial value when compared with other pages in the results. If you mainly summarize others, you add little. Add what only you can: results from your own work, photos you took, a process you follow, a mistake you made, a price you quote, or a clear opinion with reasons. Add a table, a checklist or a worked example when it helps. Do not write to a target word count. Google says it has no preferred word count. Write as long as the topic needs.

Step 7: Write so people can read it

  • Use short sentences and short paragraphs of two to three sentences.
  • Choose everyday words, and explain a term the first time you use it.
  • Use bullet points for lists and numbered steps for procedures.
  • Use active voice. Say who does what.
  • Read the draft out loud, then cut anything that does not help.

A note on scores: tools that grade reading level can help you write plainly, but Ahrefs found no correlation between Flesch Reading Ease and ranking position. Use them to help readers, not to chase a ranking. We aim for grade 8 or lower because most people read faster that way.

Step 8: Show who wrote it and why you can be trusted

Google's "Who, How and Why" test is a good checklist. It ties to what Google calls E-E-A-T: experience, expertise, authoritativeness and trust, with trust the most important. Who wrote this? Put a byline that links to a short bio with real credentials. How was it made? Say so if you used automation or AI in a major way. Why was it made? The answer should be to help people. Cite the sources you used and link to them. Only quote a statistic that you have read at the source, and say how old it is and what its limits are. Do not fake an author, use made-up credentials or hide how the post was made.

Step 9: Write a plain meta description

The meta description is a short summary that may appear under your title in search results. Google says a good one is short, unique to the page and includes the most relevant points. Keep it to about 140 to 160 characters, include the keyword once and say what the reader will get. Do not expect it to show every time. Ahrefs found that Google showed the meta description in results only 37.22% of the time and rewrote it 62.78% of the time, and that 25.02% of top-ranking pages had none. Write one anyway. It costs little, and it is your best shot at controlling the snippet.

Step 10: Use a short, clear URL

Use a slug that names the topic in a few words, such as /how-to-write-seo-friendly-blog-posts/. Use lowercase letters and hyphens. Leave out dates, extra words and IDs. Once a URL is live and earning traffic, do not change it without a redirect plan.

Step 11: Add useful links

  • Internal links: link to related posts and to the page that serves the reader's next step. Google says every page you care about should have a link from at least one other page on your site, and that there is no magic number of links. Use descriptive link text, also called anchor text, not "click here."
  • External links: link to the primary source for each statistic or claim. Link only to pages you trust. If you do not trust a page but still want to link to it, add a nofollow or similar attribute.

For example, see our guide to SEO mistakes to avoid for a checklist of problems that block good posts, and our best SEO practices for the wider picture.

Step 12: Add images with alt text

Use sharp, relevant images near the text they relate to. Add short, descriptive alt text that explains what the image shows and how it relates to the page. Leave out stuffed keywords. Compress files so the page loads quickly on a phone. Add a featured image that fits the topic, and keep each image's file name plain, such as seo-checklist-table.png.

How do you make a post useful for AI answers too?

The same habits help AI answer tools, since they pull clear, well-sourced passages. Lead each section with a direct answer, keep one idea per paragraph, use headings that match real questions, name the author, cite primary sources and show the date of the last real update. Semrush cites an AirOps study that found fresh content was one of the strongest predictors of AI visibility. That is a vendor-cited study, so treat it as a signal, not a rule. Our guide to ranking in AI Overviews goes deeper.

Should you use AI to write blog posts?

You can, with care. Google says appropriate use of AI is not against its guidelines. Using AI mainly to manipulate rankings is. Its guidance on scaled content abuse says that generating many pages without adding value for users may break its spam policy. Google also says generative models predict likely words and do not retrieve facts, so you must fact-check everything, including titles, meta descriptions and alt text. A safe approach:

  • Use AI for outlines, rewording and first drafts, not as the final author.
  • Add your own experience, examples, numbers and photos.
  • Check every fact and statistic at the source.
  • Have a named person review and own the post.
  • Do not publish dozens of near-identical pages.

See our review of AI content writing tools for options.

How often should you update a post?

Update a post when its facts change, when a better source appears, or when it starts to lose traffic. A real update means new data, new steps or a corrected claim, and a date that reflects it. Google's guidance lists changing the date of a page to make it look fresh, when the content has not substantially changed, as a warning sign. It also says that adding or removing a lot of content just to seem fresh will not help. Show the last-updated date only when you earned it.

A copyable checklist before you publish

CheckWhat good looks like
Topic and intentOne primary keyword. Matches what the top results offer.
TitleUnique, accurate, keyword near the front, about 60 characters.
OpeningAnswers the main question in two or three sentences.
HeadingsOne H1. Clear H2 and H3 headings. No skipped levels.
Original valueAt least one example, data point or experience others lack.
ReadabilityShort sentences and paragraphs. Plain words.
TrustByline, bio, sources linked, honest date.
Meta description140 to 160 characters. Unique. Says what the reader will get.
URLShort, lowercase, keyword in it.
LinksDescriptive internal links. Primary-source external links.
ImagesRelevant, compressed, with plain alt text.
Page experienceLoads fast and reads well on a phone.

A 90-minute workflow

  1. 15 minutes: choose the keyword, read the top 10 and list what is missing.
  2. 10 minutes: write the title, the answer and an outline.
  3. 40 minutes: write the draft with your own examples and sources.
  4. 15 minutes: edit for short sentences, add links and images, and write the meta description.
  5. 10 minutes: run the checklist, preview on a phone and publish.

After publishing, check Google Search Console in a few weeks. Look at impressions, clicks and the queries that bring people. Improve the post based on what you see.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Writing for the keyword, not the reader. Stuffing a phrase into every line hurts readability and trust.
  • Copying the top results. If you add nothing new, there is no reason to rank above them.
  • Publishing thin posts. Short, vague pages rarely earn traffic.
  • Skipping the byline and sources. They are quick trust signals.
  • Faking freshness. Changing the date without changing the content can backfire.
  • Ignoring mobile. A slow, cramped page loses readers.
  • Not measuring. Without data, you cannot improve.

Worked example (illustrative, not a client result)

Take a hypothetical accounting firm that wants to rank for "how to track small business expenses." It reads the top 10 results and finds mostly generic lists with no examples. It chooses a how-to format, adds a downloadable sheet, a worked example with sample numbers it can support, and a short section on mistakes it sees with new clients. The title is "How to Track Small Business Expenses: A Simple 5-Step Method." The post opens with the answer, names the partner who wrote it, links to the tax authority's rules and to two of the firm's own pages, and adds a clear call to book a review. No traffic numbers are claimed, because this is a template. The point is the process: study the results, add original value, then build the page cleanly.

Our interest in this topic

Reinforce Lab sells SEO and content services. Nothing here is paid placement. Jamil Ahmed, who wrote this guide, is a Semrush Ambassador, and Reinforce Lab uses affiliate links for some tools. Read our FTC and affiliate disclosure. Our SEO content systems service follows these steps, and you can get your free diagnostic.

Final thoughts

SEO friendly blog posts are not a formula. They are useful posts with clean signals. Choose a topic worth your reader's time, check what already ranks, add something new, and make the page clear and trustworthy. Measure what happens, and keep the post true as things change.

Ideas for Personal Website Content, Personal Website Content Ideas, Content Ideas for Personal Website

post_content:
Having creative ideas for personal website content can go a long way to progressing your career, as a website is more unique than a CV or resume.

Whether you are hunting for work, trying to run a business, or selling a product, a website of your own can provide you with a healthy online presence and more credibility.

Anyone can open a page on a social media platform or business/employment platforms that are readily available. 

However, having your own website would indicate that you are more serious. 

So with all the business and industry websites around us, let’s get to know about:

 

What is a Personal Website?

 

A personal website is a website created to showcase an individual’s work and persona.

Unlike the majority of internet web pages, it does not pertain to any particular corporation, institution, or organization.

You can denote it as a group of web pages where only your personal features, works, achievements, and contact information will be.

 

Additionally, it lets you showcase your work in your creative structure.

WorkItDaily states that nearly 56% of employers and recruiters are more impressed by an individual’s website.

On the other hand, according to Forbes, only 7% of the general population has a personal website. For millennials, the percentage is 15%. 

Of course, the percentages have increased by today.

Nonetheless, it indicates that a personal website can give you a great chance to stand out from the crowd.

Having a personal website might sound difficult at first, however, once you get the hang of it, it is pretty straightforward.

Furthermore, when you develop some personal website content ideas and implement them in a well-planned way, it creates a beautiful online presence for you.

To implement that more effectively, you can look into some simple personal website examples for ideas.

You will be able to see how creatively people have already managed to showcase their features.

Usually, you will find many colorful and vibrant features in their web content design.

Moreover, if you are more serious about your work and focusing on a professional presence, you can look into some professional personal website examples. 

Checking these out will give you a more in-depth idea about web content personalization in a more professional manner.

At the end of the day, you want to create a healthy online presence and attract people who are more aligned or appreciative of your work.

Your personal website design and personal website content allow you to do just that.

It is a great source of personal branding.

With those in mind, we are here to provide you with some amazing ideas for personal website content.

 

Ideas for Personal Website Content

 

The more decorated, organized, and personalized your personal website content is, the more attractive it will feel.

You will even feel good about yourself when your website is full of quality content.

So, with a focus on web content personalization, here are the sections and content you must have on your website for proper optimization.

Homepage

 

Your website homepage should greet people according to your persona and profession.

Decorate your homepage with your signature style, font, and colors. 

If your homepage layout is strong, so will your website.

Personal websites do not need a lot of links and sub-links.

We will explain which sections and pages will add more to your website.

However, make it so that your homepage itself will catch the eyes of the hiring managers.

Add attractive feature photos of you or content related to you.

You can also include an image of your workstation if you make it visually organized and pleasing. Look out for the color scheme.

Choosing an aesthetically pleasing color scheme for your website will highly appeal to the visual memory of your potential clients.

Include your elevator pitch statement on your homepage.

It means mentioning your passion, profession, and goal in your way.

On your homepage, do it as shortly and impactfully as possible.

This, when done effectively, will lead your visitors to be interested to learn more about you.

Needless to say, your homepage is the most integral part of your personal website design.

It will define the template of your website and lead site visitors to more of your personalized website content.

 

About Page

 

Having a crafty, short, and sweet About page will give people just what they need. An idea of you and your work.

Oftentimes, it would be the home page or landing page of your website, so make a good first impression.

Don’t make the mistake of making your about page too long.

It may have worked in the early stages on the internet. 

In today’s day and age, just having a short greeting, having a bit of personal touch, and showcasing your work and background would be enough.

Just feature these:

  • What do you work on
  • Your educational/professional background
  • A mentionable work achievement
  • Your latest project and current passion

All these pieces of information can make your About Page good to go.

This page is another sector where you are endorsing your elevator pitch.

So, make your passion and profession known to your site visitors.

Let them know what you are looking for and aiming for. All these can make your about page much stronger.

 

Contact Info

 

So now that people know about you, where can they contact you, or how can they hire you?

It is essential to let people connect with you and contact you. In that regard, attach your email and contact number if you feel comfortable.

Link your social or professional profiles as required.

It is a good idea to attach appropriate icons with the contacts.

This makes the contact content look more familiar, professional, and attractive.

A great piece of content you can create for your website is a contact form.

People can leave text messages directly there or if they have any inquiries.

It is always best to let people choose multiple options to contact you.

Whether they want to email you, text you, or contact you directly, they should have the option. 

So craft your contact information content section accordingly.

 

Portfolio

 

Your portfolio will need to feature your best work samples. This gives your viewer a hands-on experience of your work.

Visual content creator like graphic designers or photo/video editors can make their best impression in this sector.

So, if you are a graphic designer or editor, do not forget to put in your best work here to showcase to the world.

If you are a content writer or web developer, you can link your best articles and web pages here.

If you send your website to your possible employers, this is where they would focus most.

So it is very necessary to make your personal website’s portfolio section well-crafted and organized.

 

Resume

 

Forwarding a regular resume through email or hand-to-hand has become a common experience nowadays.

However, if you pass your website to your potential client or employer, it creates a different experience when they see your resume on your website.

You can take help from resume websites.

From there, you can easily form and share your resume using proper templates.

Make sure these sections are visible in your resume:

  • Your education/ qualifications
  • Your skillsets and expertise
  • Your work experiences
  • Your notable achievements

These pieces of content are very necessary for your resume, which adds to your site too.

Usually, you would add specific changes to your resume according to the need of the job you are applying for.

Since on your website, anyone from any sector can visit your resume, you can make your resume a bit more elaborate.

Try to include all your noteworthy educational and professional qualifications in your resume so that it can seem multipurpose and cover multiple grounds.

 

Professional Blogs

 

Blogs should be included in your personal website content ideas.

Blogs contain a lot of useful information and, if presented well, also generate a lot of traffic.

So whether you write your article or feature some blog articles related to your profession, it would surely enrich your personal website and make it look well-established.

Link your WordPress with your website.

Learn how to function and operate WordPress well.

Through that, you will easily be able to process, update, write, and re-write articles to your liking.

People regularly visit blogs for updates, tips, information, and fun.

So when you have well-crafted, relevant, and engaging blogs on your website, your personal website quality and viewership will automatically skyrocket.

People often comment in blog comment sections. Look after those.

Interact with them, and you will also find possible new ideas for newer content.

 

Testimonials

 

Positive word of mouth is always a plus for any personal or business venture. 

When clients or employers check your website and see authentic reviews and words from people who have worked with you or people you have worked for, it is sure to create a positive impact.

Beyond what you write about yourself, if people agree that you have a strong work ethic, you are skilled and expert in your sector, and all the related adjectives relevant to your sector, it can give you increased credibility.

To garner authentic testimonials, you can ask your formal clients and or employers to mention a brief comment about yourself and how helpful your work or skillset has been.

If they struggle to write properly, use a formal LinkedIn comment that goes with you and ask for their approval or modification.

All in all, testimonials are surely very useful among your ideas for personal website content.

 

Case Studies

 

Case studies analyze the reports of your products or services in a more detailed manner than testimonials.

So these can be even more effective than mere reviews. 

Case studies can make your website and personal profile even more credible and influence your site visitors to work with you.

It is a kind of social proof that eliminates any of your hiring managers’ doubt or trust issues.

In conclusion, case studies can be pretty effective.

 

What type of Content to Avoid for A Personal Website?

 

It is to be mentioned that while you already have some idea about what to do and not to do, it is good to be reminded so that you are aware.

Pay close attention to these points-

  • Make your about page too lengthy and uneventful
  • Don’t overwhelm your viewer or site visitors with too many collections of your work and history details. Keep some things to yourself, and focus on featuring the best ones.
  • Avoid mentioning social media platforms that are unrelated to your work and profession. 
  • Do not post images that are low in resolution or stolen from stock photos.
  • Do not post blogs that are poorly researched or misleading.
  • Do not be inconsistent with your blog posts. Regularly updating them would make your website seem more active and fresh.
  • Do not post vague testimonials that might be full of mistakes and overly flattering. Make sure they are written accordingly with approval. Keep them work-specific and simple.
  • If you feel like you can not write updated, thought-provoking blogs free of many mistakes, it is better to avoid them. If a visitor comes to your site and sees that your last post was two years ago, they can automatically assume that your website is outdated.

 

Wrapping Up: Ideas for Personal Website Content

 

It can understandably seem hard to establish a personal website at first. However, with these ideas for personal website content, you will start to feel more confident about what you can post.

The world is open to you on the internet, and through your personal website, you can connect and engage more people than ever before. 

So utilize these personal website content ideas, and make your progress come to you.

 

Liked what you read? There’s more to be learned!

Your website is one of your most prominent marketing channels. So, you must know these 10 ways of marketing for websites for your better growth.

As a business owner, if you already have an established website, you know how much effort and hope you have behind your empire.

However, if you do not know how to market your website better on the internet, how can you possibly hope to reach those dreams and goals?

That is why it is a must for your marketing campaign to have marketing strategies for your website.

Marketing for a website is a not-so-daunting task.

Social media and other digital platforms have grown immensely. They have also become more available and accessible to everyone.

So, your opportunity of marketing for a website has increased tenfold.

You just need to be aware of these tremendous opportunities.

Just because of a prior lack of experience, many business owners keep wandering in a circle.

However, you do not wish to be among them. That is why you are here.

So here we are to make you familiar with what marketing for websites truly means.

You will be able to find out why marketing for a website is so important.

And additionally, you will be able to understand what are the perfect ways of marketing a website.

Furthermore, you will have some must-have website marketing strategies and website marketing ideas.

You can jot them down for sure success, as a written vision of your strategy is very important.

So lets begin with the question, what is marketing for websites? Do you understand website marketing properly?

 

What Is Marketing for Websites?

 

Marketing for websites means the process of promoting your website(s) on other platforms.

Your website should appear on the search engines as long as your webpage is minimally optimized.

If you have a proper description and navigation structure for your website, search engines would promote it automatically.

However, search engine optimization is only a part of it now. You need to think one step ahead of the competition.

The vast majority of marketing for websites is already conveyed through experienced marketing strategy templates. You can not through them away either.

So your marketing for website should be a mixture of the old along with the new.

Old Marketing Strategies

You need to integrate what worked before. Offline marketing like TV commercials or billboards can increase exposure, but will only get you so far.

Direct affiliate marketing is also a core marketing idea. However, you need the recent marketing strategies even more.

New Marketing Strategies

In modern times, search engine optimization (SEO), Email marketing, all of these will hold their places.

In addition, capitalizing on social media marketing, PPC marketing, Video marketing, and other sorts of content marketing will really help your campaign.

Regardless, your website marketing campaign should be written down. What you have in your head needs to be neatly visualized for others to see.

It is a great way to make your visions come true. Otherwise, you could be in a “ship without a radar” scenario.

So not to forget, you need to 1. Have a strategy planned out, 2. Need to integrate the old with the new, 3. Keep up with the competition and do it before them.

All things considered, we know you are wondering, how do I get customers to your website?

The first thing of course would be to cater to your customers.

After you have found your potential customers and target audience, it is your duty to create your own unique personal website.

You can learn more from our article Best 5 Ideas for Personal Website Content.

If you are branding your personal website, this will help you understand what you can put up on your website.

If you are a business owner, there will be more to learn about how do you market a website.

We are elaborating upon that in the section below.

 

How Do You Market A Website?

 

The first thing you need to do will be to identify your target audience.

Your potential customers are ready to buy. In addition, you must have it pictured in your mind who are your target audience.

So you should definitely include it in a written format when you are plotting your business marketing strategy.

Furthermore, definitely make your website interface unique and attractive.

Otherwise even a strong marketing campaign might fail.

Afterward, you can take advantage of the core ways of website marketing.

Your website SEO, Email Marketing, Blogging, Social Media Marketing, and much more would be included in this.

Now let us get into the nitty gritty of your marketing strategies for websites.

These 10 website marketing ideas will not only help you stay relevant but will also help you to move ahead.

That way you can attract more traffic to your site, reach out to more potential customers, and get familiar with the proper marketing tool or tools you need to use.

In time, you will be a pro at social media marketing. In addition, your social media platforms will have an automated stream of marketable content.

10 Perfect Ways of Marketing for Websites

 

1. Perform a Website Design Review

 

Your website is like the window for your shopping cart.

So as any shop ever created, it should look neat, clean, and decently decorated from the outside.

On the inside, it should look well organized, so everything is found accordingly.

So just like a shop, is a website a form of marketing?

Of course, it is!

That is how your website should also actually be.

To take care of these, you need to keep these simple things in mind.

Have A Proper Website and UX Design

Just like in a shop, your customers would not like to get confused traveling around in isles without directions.

Similarly, your website should also have a proper UX design. With proper navigation, copywriting, and design, your website’s user experience is sure to increase.

A Simple Website Structure

Make sure your website’s site structure has a simple hierarchy.

Any webpage should not take more than 3 clicks to reach from your homepage to access.

Proper Information

Additionally, make sure it has all the accurate information about your business, products, and services.

Mobile-friendly and Loading Time

Last but not least, try to make sure your website is mobile-friendly and your website’s loading time is decreased.

Many visitors scroll blogs or websites from the comfort of their smartphones on the go nowadays.

So a mobile-friendly site structure would keep you ahead.

Your landing page should also take minimal time to load to increase

Of course, if you manage to increase user experience, you will have more acquired customers in addition to retaining customers.

You can find out more about UX copywriting from our blog The Ultimate Guide to UX Copywriting 2025.

 

2. Make Your Site SEO Optimized

 

You must have an SEO strategy for your website as a lot of traffic is garnered solely from search engines.

Search Engine Optimization SEO for short is the process that helps you rank.

Nowadays, it is not only limited to search engine results, but social media platforms also follow SEO.

Increasing your website’s visibility will definitely increase exposure, traffic, familiarity, and in time, more conversions and sales.

So focus SEO on these factors.

SEO Content

Whether you are writing a blog, a caption, or a description, try to make sure your writing has all the necessary keywords.

Local SEO

Chances are, you do not have an international business. So you should optimize your website according to your region of jurisdiction.

Location-aware searches will help you get the customers you can actually serve or deliver products to.

So plan your SEO accordingly to capitalize on it.

On-Page SEO

Google searches and similar search engines use web crawlers. These are bots that help the search engines find out which contents need to be featured in their search result.

Your duty to improve on-page SEO is to understand how these crawlers can find your website, your article, and your content.

Properly understand the keyword usage and search volumes of the keywords to make your webpages SEO-friendly. Also, make your content easy to read and accessible.

A combination of these will make your on-page SEO on point.

Off-Page SEO

As we have already mentioned, search engines crawl your website to check relativity, authenticity, and authority.

Outside of your content, the number of referrals or links you have from other websites also improves your SEO.

If other websites provide links to your website or articles, those also boost authority in search results.

These are all part of your off-page SEO, which you do not do on your webpage directly.

Getting these connections and links can really help boosting your site image and it is an integral part of your website marketing strategy.

 

3. Social Media Optimization

 

Just like you use your website as a marketing tool, you can use social media as a tool for marketing your website.

In the previous segment, we have already mentioned that social media marketing is unavoidable for growth in today’s world.

Furthermore, SEO also improves your social media exposure.

With that in mind, you should definitely optimize your social media content for SEO too.

It is a good strategy to drive traffic to your website which you can feature on your social media platforms.

You can follow the following process for better improvement of your marketing strategy.

Make A Business Account

Having a business account will allow you to promote your website more prominently and frequently.

Make A Social Media Calendar

Your social media reach and success also depends on your regularity of posting.

Having quality content on a regular basis will clearly indicate more reliability.

Just create a written schedule for when you want to post what type of content.

This will keep you focused and give you a head-start.

Add Your Website Links to Your Page and Profile

Since you want to promote your website, this is something you must not forget.

Whenever you find it relevant, take the opportunity to provide the link to your website for more details.

This is a great website marketing strategy example to capitalize on.

Grow Your Following

Through regular posting and following the aforementioned process, you will reach your target audience even better.

Growing your target audience will also grow your followers, and eventually will drive more traffic to your website.

All these are great strategies of marketing for websites on social media.

 

4. Email Marketing

 

Email marketing has been working charms for blogs and websites for a long before.

So having an elaborate email list for your website marketing campaign should also be on your strategy.

People still have strong connections with their emails, especially in business and professional sectors. So do not think email is dead.

It can be great to drive traffic back to your website, let people know what’s new, or pitch them a product directly.

 

5. Use Paid Ads

 

While SEO and other optimizing factors might take some time to rank, a small paid ad campaign can really help you reach visitors and customers faster.

You can use Google Ads as an advertising platform.

That way your website will get featured on the platforms partnered with Google AdSense.

This includes paid ads on Google search results, Gmail, YouTube, etc.

You can also capitalize on Facebook Ads to feature your Facebook page or posts.

You can also use the following:

  • Google Local Service Ads
  • Advertising on Angi
  • Yelp for Business Ads
  • Microsoft Advertising (formerly Bing Ads)

If you have video content related to your website, those can also be featured through paid ad campaigns.

 

6. Use Video Content
